findings.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner requires the caller to be BOTH team admin AND team owner (&&) where the variable name and intent say OR, so plain team admins/owners are rejected. A team admin who is not also an owner clicks Additional Guests, adds emails, hits Add and receives FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission'; since a membership has one role, if isTeamAdmin strictly matches ADMIN the isTeamAdminOrOwner branch is false for every user and no team member can ever add guests, leaving only the booking organizer/attendee paths.

[BUG] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) runs with id 0 for bookings whose userId is null and throws an unhandled Prisma P2025. Adding guests to a pending round-robin booking (userId null, booker passes the isAttendee check) crashes with an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError surfaced as tRPC INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR 500 instead of a typed error.

[BUG] blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but each guest email is compared raw (both the blacklist includes and the existing-attendee duplicate check), making the comparisons case-sensitive. An operator's BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry is bypassed by changing letter case (e.g. User@Example.com against a lowercased blacklist), and a case-variant of an existing attendee email passes the 'unique' filter, creating a duplicate attendee row for the same person on one booking.

[BUG] The EventManager is built from the CALLER's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and {...user}) while evt.organizer and evt.destinationCalendar belong to the BOOKING organizer, so calendar attendee updates are attempted with the wrong user's credentials. When a permitted non-organizer caller adds guests (the booker as attendee, or a team member passing the role check), CalendarManager finds no credential matching the organizer's destinationCalendar and updateCalendarAttendees silently no-ops, so the organizer's Google/Outlook event never gains the new guests while the UI reports success.

[BUG] The sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in a catch that discards the error object (catch (err) with err unused, only a bare console.log string) and the handler unconditionally returns success. When SMTP/email delivery fails, every recipient (new guests included) receives nothing, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast with no retry path, and the only server trace is 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' with no error detail.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input array guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so email-manager's newGuests.includes(attendee.email) test counts already-filtered emails as new. When a mixed list contains an email already attending the booking (which client-side validation cannot detect), that existing attendee is resent a full AttendeeScheduledEmail 'your event has been scheduled' email instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice intended for non-new attendees.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is only reset by the Cancel button; neither the Dialog onOpenChange close path (ESC/X) nor the mutation onSuccess resets it. After one failed attempt (or after a failed attempt followed by a later successful add), reopening the dialog shows the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error over a pristine empty form until Cancel is clicked.

[ADVISORY] In onError, message is a template literal (always truthy) so the 'unable_to_add_guests' fallback in showToast(message || t('unable_to_add_guests')) is dead code, and err.data is undefined for non-TRPC errors. Users with a network/timeout failure get a toast reading 'undefined: Network request failed'-style text, and the intended generic 'Unable to add guests' message can never render; maintainers editing the fallback will find it unreachable.

[ADVISORY] handleAdd silently early-returns when multiEmailValue is an empty array, which is reachable by clicking the row's remove addon until no rows remain. A user who deletes every row and clicks Add gets zero feedback (no toast, no validation banner), leaving an Add button that appears broken; the 'Add Emails' state button reappears in the body but the footer action is dead.

[ADVISORY] The guest validation schema is hand-duplicated between this dialog (z.array + uniqueness refine) and addGuests.schema.ts on the server, and the two copies already diverge behaviorally: the client only rejects in-array duplicates while the server silently de-duplicates against existing attendees and blacklist entries. A user who submits a mix of one new and one already-attending email sees 'Guests added' with no indication that one email was silently skipped, and any future rule (max guests, blacklist awareness) must be implemented twice or the layers drift further.

[ADVISORY] The remove control's tooltip hardcodes the English string "Remove email" while every other string in the component goes through t(). Non-English users of the new Add Guests dialog see an untranslated English tooltip on the row-remove button in every locale until the string is moved into common.json.

[ADVISORY] New guest attendee records are created with name: "" and no name is ever derived (e.g. from the email address). New guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail and an .ics whose attendee name is empty (greeting like 'Hi ,' and CN="" on the calendar invite), and the stored attendee rows carry blank names for any future feature that renders attendee lists.

[ADVISORY] The entire new mutation (permission matrix, blacklist filtering, dedup, calendar/email fan-out) plus the new dialog has no test anywhere in this diff. Regressions in the permission logic and filtering ship silently — the && permission bug at lines 46-48 and the case-sensitivity blacklist bypass at lines 70-78 are exactly the class of defect a permission-matrix test would have caught before release.

[BUG] The team permission gate uses `&&`, requiring the user to be BOTH admin and owner simultaneously, contradicting the variable's own name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. A team admin who is not an owner (and any owner, if isTeamAdmin excludes the OWNER role) selects 'additional_guests' on a team booking and receives FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, silently breaking the feature for exactly the roles the code claims to grant.

[BUG] Blacklist entries are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but the guest input is compared un-lowercased (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so any case-variant email bypasses the blacklist. An operator configures BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='banned@example.com', a user submits 'Banned@Example.com', and the banned address is created as an attendee and sent full booking details plus a CONFIRMED ICS — the control only ever blocks exact-lowercase matches.

[ADVISORY] The existing-attendee dedupe uses case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email`, so a case-variant of an already-present attendee email passes the filter. A user adds 'Bob@Example.com' when 'bob@example.com' is already an attendee; createMany inserts a duplicate attendee row and the attendee receives duplicate emails and appears twice in calendar attendee lists.

[BUG] The server schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` omits the uniqueness refine the client enforces (AddGuestsDialog.tsx lines 26-29), and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only removes emails matching existing attendees, never duplicates within the request array. Any authed client calls viewer.bookings.addGuests with guests:['a@x.com','a@x.com'] (bypassing the dialog's refine), createMany inserts two identical attendee rows and sendAddGuestsEmails dispatches two scheduled emails to the same address, corrupting the booking's attendee list.

[BUG] The guests array has no `.max()` bound and the handler enforces no count limit, while the mutation fans out to a createMany, a calendar API update, and one email per attendee per call. Any authed attendee (the permission gate grants every attendee of a booking) submits tens of thousands of emails in a single mutation, inserting that many attendee rows and launching an unbounded Promise.all of email sends — a DB and mail-pipeline exhaustion vector.

[BUG] The organizer lookup runs `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` — the `|| 0` guard proves the author expects userId to be null sometimes, and id 0 never matches, so it throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 error. A requester who passes permission via the isAttendee check on a booking with null userId gets an unhandled PrismaNotFoundError surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with a raw Prisma message in the toast instead of any 4xx.

[BUG] The booking is fetched with only `{ id: bookingId }` and booking.status is never checked, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING (requiresConfirmation) bookings. A user adds guests to a cancelled booking; those guests receive 'New guests added to your event' emails carrying a method=REQUEST status=CONFIRMED ICS for a meeting that no longer exists and accept phantom calendar entries.

[BUG] The CalendarEvent constructed here never sets `team`, yet sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts lines 531-537) sends team-member notifications only inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)`. For every round-robin/team booking the team branch is dead code — fellow team members never receive the Guests Added notification the email-manager clearly intends, and no error is raised anywhere because the only caller never populates team.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the requesting user (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) even though the booking query at lines 35-40 already fetched booking.user.credentials, so calendar updates run with the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's. When an attendee or team admin — explicitly permitted by the permission gate — adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's connected calendar and silently no-ops: the organizer's Google/Outlook event never gains the guests while the UI reports 'Guests added'.

[BUG] `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw request array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so the email-manager's `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check (email-manager.ts line 541) matches emails that were filtered out and never added. When the request contains an already-attendee's email (silently dropped by the uniqueGuests filter), that existing attendee receives the full AttendeeScheduledEmail 'your event has been scheduled' email instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice — a wrong, confusing email for an event they booked long ago.

[ADVISORY] Email delivery failure is swallowed by `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — the error object is discarded and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. When the SMTP/mail provider fails, guests and organizer are never notified yet the user sees the success toast 'Guests added', and the single console.log without the error leaves operators unable to diagnose the lost invites.

[ADVISORY] Guests filtered out by the uniqueGuests check (already an attendee, blacklisted, or case-variant) are dropped with no per-email feedback — the response is a hardcoded 'Guests added' regardless of how many were skipped. An organizer submits two emails where one is already an attendee; the toast says 'Guests added', the skipped person is neither added nor notified, and the organizer assumes the colleague is on the booking and misses the meeting.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a 174-line mutation handler containing an authorization matrix, blacklist filtering, dedupe, and email-type dispatch, and adds zero tests — no test-shaped file appears anywhere in the diff for any of the new logic. The permission-operator bug at lines 46-48 and the wrong-array email bug at line 168 in this very diff ship undetected; the next refactor regresses authorization or email routing with no CI signal, and the 'only organizer/attendee/team-admin can add guests' acceptance criterion is verified nowhere.

[ADVISORY] The `add_members` menu entry is appended to the dropdown with no permission gating, while the handler denies everyone except the organizer, an attendee, and (admin && owner). A plain team member viewing team bookings sees 'additional_guests', opens the dialog, submits valid emails, and gets a FORBIDDEN error toast — a visible UI action that can never succeed for them.

[ADVISORY] A new operator-facing env var BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is introduced with no accompanying .env.example entry, documentation page, or settings surface anywhere in the diff. Self-hosted operators never learn the blacklist exists, so the only administrative control over who may be added as a guest goes unconfigured on every self-hosted instance.

[BUG] `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on validation failure but never reset in the mutation's onSuccess (which resets only multiEmailValue) nor on dialog close via onOpenChange — only the Cancel button clears it. After one failed validation the user corrects the email and submits successfully; the next time they open the dialog for any booking, the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner is displayed over a pristine empty form.

[ADVISORY] The remove button's tooltip is the hardcoded English string `content="Remove email"` in a component that otherwise translates via `t('add_another')`. Every non-English locale shows an untranslated English tooltip on the remove action, in the same PR that carefully added five new translation keys for this feature.

[ADVISORY] For seat-based event types the handler copies seatsPerTimeSlot into the CalendarEvent (line 145) but never validates that adding the new guests keeps the booking within its seat capacity before createMany. On a 5-seat event type an attendee adds 10 guests in one call; the booking now holds 15 attendee rows against 5 seats with no error, breaking seat-based availability and per-seat attendee handling.

[BUG] The team-permission gate combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && although the variable name (isTeamAdminOrOwner) and the gate's purpose require ||, and since a team membership holds a single role, the conjunction cannot pass a plain team admin. A team admin who is not also the team owner (and is neither the booking's organizer nor an attendee) is rejected with FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission', so the team path of the guest-management feature is dead for the entire admin role the check was written to serve.

[BUG] The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client dialog enforces, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-78) only removes emails already on the booking, so duplicate emails within one request pass validation and reach prisma createMany (lines 100-106). A direct tRPC mutation with guests ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] — the endpoint is authedProcedure, reachable by any logged-in user without the dialog — inserts two identical BookingAttendee rows: the attendee appears twice in the ICS attachment and receives duplicate copies of every guest email, permanently corrupting the booking's attendee list.

[BUG] The blacklist comparison lowercases only the configured list (line 71) and never the guest string, and the existing-attendee check at line 76 is an exact-case ===, so both guards are case-sensitive. Submitting 'Spam@Example.com' against a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry 'spam@example.com' (or against an attendee stored as 'spam@example.com') bypasses both the blacklist and the duplicate filter, creating and emailing a guest the operator explicitly blocked.

[ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed from the requesting session user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) rather than the booking organizer's credentials, even though the handler loads booking.user with credentials (include at lines 35-40) and never uses them. On the attendee- or team-admin-initiated paths that the permission gate (lines 46-56) exists to enable, updateCalendarAttendees runs holding the caller's credentials, which lack the organizer's connected Google/Outlook calendar, so new guests never land on the organizer's external event while the mutation still returns 'Guests added' — a silent partial failure.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw request input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so emails deliberately dropped as already-attendees are still treated as new in email-manager.ts's template selection (newGuests.includes(attendee.email) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail). A user who re-submits a list containing one already-invited email triggers a full 'you are scheduled' AttendeeScheduledEmail to that existing attendee — a duplicate booking confirmation for an event they already hold — instead of the guests-added notice.

[ADVISORY] The uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch reuses the validation string 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' for the unrelated condition 'every submitted email is already an attendee or blacklisted'. An organizer re-adding an existing guest sees 'Emails must be unique and valid' over input that is both unique and valid, with no hint the email is already on the booking, so the error is unactionable and the add flow appears broken.

[ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails logs the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards err entirely, while the mutation still returns success. When SMTP or template rendering fails, operators get a log line with no error object, stack, or booking identifier, and the caller sees the 'guests_added' success toast — guests silently receive nothing and the failure cannot be diagnosed from logs.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure (line 56) but never reset — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not the flag, and the dialog stays mounted in BookingListItem so state survives close/reopen. After a single failed attempt, the red 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' banner is still displayed when the user reopens the dialog (same or another booking) over an empty, valid form, and it remains visible after a subsequent successful add — a stale validation error contradicting the visible state.

[BUG] The organizer lookup runs prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0, which throws a raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError (P2025) when booking.userId is null — a state the evt construction itself defends against via booking?.user?. guards (lines 140-144). Any caller who passes the permission gate via the attendee or team path on a booking with an unassigned organizer (nullable userId in the schema) gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx TRPCError, after the booking was already fetched and authorized.

[ADVISORY] The booking query filters only on id, with no predicate on status or endTime, so cancelled, rejected, and past bookings are all valid targets for addGuests. Guests (and a CONFIRMED 'REQUEST' ics file) can be attached to a booking the organizer already cancelled, delivering calendar invites that resurrect the cancelled event in every recipient's calendar.

[ADVISORY] The dialog hand-duplicates ZAddGuestsInputSchema (z.array(z.string().email()) plus a uniqueness refine) instead of sharing one schema definition with the server's addGuests.schema.ts, and the copies have already drifted — the server schema has no uniqueness refine. Every future change to guest validation (max count, email normalization, format) must be applied in two hand-maintained places; the uniqueness divergence in this very diff is the first instance of client and server enforcing different rules, and the next divergence ships silently.

[ADVISORY] BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS introduces new operator-facing behavior with no .env.example entry, documentation, or admin surface anywhere in the diff. Self-hosted operators cannot discover the guest blacklist exists, so the guard ships inert in every deployment whose admins don't read handler source; even operators who find it get no documented format contract, which is how the case-sensitivity bypass at lines 74-78 goes unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships a 174-line mutation whose entire security posture is the hand-rolled gate at lines 46-56 (admin/owner/organizer/attendee) plus blacklist and dedupe filtering, with no test file touching any of it. The &&-for-|| permission defect in this same gate shipped precisely because no test exercises the team-admin path; the next edit to these lines either locks out a permitted role or opens guest-adding to any logged-in user, with nothing in CI to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The guest-management dialog seeds MultiEmail with [''] and never fetches or displays the booking's current guests, so the user adds blind. An organizer returning to invite one more guest cannot see who is already on the booking, re-submits an overlapping list, and lands in the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error path — the add flow cannot be completed correctly on a second visit without guessing.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner for the team-permission path to grant access. A team ADMIN who is not the owner gets FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') when adding guests to their own team's bookings, and if isTeamAdmin matches only the ADMIN role then even owners fail the team check — the permission path named 'AdminOrOwner' never works for the admin class it was written for, breaking the feature for every non-owner team admin.

[BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, so the two copies of the same validation already disagree in this diff. Any caller other than this dialog (direct tRPC mutation, API client, or a stale bundle) sending guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation, and createMany inserts two identical Attendee rows for one person, who then receives duplicate emails and appears twice in the calendar event; the client-side guard was the only thing preventing it.

[BUG] guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() bound, and the handler fans each guest out into a DB row, a confirmation email, and calendar/ICS updates. Any permitted caller — including a mere attendee of any booking, since isAttendee grants access — can submit thousands of emails in a single mutation, forcing an unbounded createMany plus an unbounded email and external calendar fan-out on one request with no rate or count limit anywhere in the path.

[BUG] The duplicate check reads booking.attendees (lines 74-78) and then inserts in a separate update with no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email) — a check-then-insert TOCTOU with nothing backing it at the schema level. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking and the same email both pass the filter and both execute createMany, producing duplicate Attendee rows that no constraint forbids; the same missing invariant also lets any other write path create the same duplicate.

[BUG] The dedup filter compares raw guest strings with exact equality (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist in the same expression lowercases its entries — normalization is applied asymmetrically within one filter. Resubmitting an already-attendee email in different casing (John@X.com vs stored john@x.com) slips past the duplicate filter and creates a second Attendee row for the same person (duplicate emails, double calendar invite); the same asymmetry means the lowercased blacklist never matches a mixed-case guest string.

[BUG] organizer is fetched with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }) while Booking.userId is nullable, and the permission gate above explicitly lets plain attendees reach this line. For any booking with a null userId, an attendee who passes the isAttendee check hits findFirstOrThrow on id 0, which throws an unhandled PrismaClientNotFoundError — the client gets a raw 500 instead of a clean error, after already being told they had permission.

[BUG] The handler validates only caller identity — never booking.status or booking times — before creating attendees and dispatching CONFIRMED invitations, and BookingListItem adds the 'additional_guests' menu item unconditionally for every booking row. Guests can be added to CANCELLED and past bookings; the new guests then receive a full booking-confirmation email with a status:CONFIRMED ICS for an event that no longer exists, and the cancelled booking's attendee list is permanently mutated.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed from the requesting user (ctx.user) and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), but evt.destinationCalendar belongs to the booking's organizer (booking.user), so the credentials never match the calendar being updated when requester != organizer. When a non-organizer (an attendee or team admin — exactly the callers the permission model allows) adds guests, the EventManager holds the requester's credentials, finds no credential for the organizer's destination calendar, and the external Google/Outlook calendar event is silently left without the new attendees while the mutation returns 'Guests added'.

[BUG] The isAttendee permission check compares attendee.email === user.email with exact case-sensitive string equality, though attendee emails are stored exactly as typed at booking time. A user whose account email casing differs from the mixed-case email they booked with (attendee rows are not normalized) is denied with FORBIDDEN even though they are a legitimate attendee of the booking, while the same email matched case-insensitively elsewhere in the codebase.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input list instead of uniqueGuests, so emails that were filtered out of creation still drive the new-guest classification (newGuests.includes) in email-manager. An existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (filtered from creation) matches newGuests.includes(attendee.email) and receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail 'your booking is confirmed' email again instead of the 'new guests added' notice — a duplicate re-confirmation for someone who was not re-added.

[BUG] The mutation is non-idempotent and its error vocabulary conflates 'no new emails' with 'invalid emails': when every submitted email already exists on the booking, uniqueGuests is empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. After any post-commit failure (the uncaught updateCalendarAttendees throw at line 165, or a client timeout) the guests are already persisted but the user sees an error; clicking Add again deterministically returns 'emails must be unique and valid' for emails that were valid and were in fact already added, so the user is told their correct input is invalid while the operation actually succeeded.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails loops over calendarEvent.team.members, but its only caller (addGuestsHandler) builds the CalendarEvent literal without any team property, so this branch can never execute in the new flow. Team members of team bookings are silently never notified when guests are added — the loop is dead code that will mislead the next maintainer into believing team notifications happen; either populate evt.team in the handler or delete the branch.

[ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "" and then receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail confirmation template via the newGuests classification in email-manager. Every newly added guest's confirmation email (and the ICS attendee entry) greets a blank name — 'Hi ,' with no recipient name — on every single add-guests call, since there is no fallback (e.g. email local part) anywhere in the path.

[ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees into evt, showing seat-based event types are in scope, but never enforces seat capacity and creates plain Attendee rows with no BookingSeat records. An organizer of a seats event adds unlimited guests past seatsPerTimeSlot with no check, and those guests bypass BookingSeat-based capacity and seat-cancellation accounting while still inflating attendee lists used by emails and ICS — the seat invariant the schema elsewhere maintains is unenforced on this new write path.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||, so it is true only for users who are simultaneously team admin and team owner, silently inverting the OR that the variable's own name declares. A team admin who is not also the team owner (and a team owner without a separate admin membership) calling viewer.bookings.addGuests on a team booking is rejected with FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, so the intended 'admin or owner may manage guests' permission path is dead code — and the diff ships no test that would have caught it.

[BUG] Blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71 but the guest value is compared unnormalized on line 77, so blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) never matches a mixed-case submission. An operator who sets BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=user@example.com watches User@Example.com pass the filter, get persisted as a booking attendee, and receive the event email — the abuse-prevention control is defeated by any case variation.

[BUG] uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees and the blacklist and never dedupes within the input guests array, so the uniqueness invariant the feature promises is enforced only by the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog. A direct viewer.bookings.addGuests mutation with ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the handler and reaches prisma createMany on line 101, persisting two identical attendee rows (or aborting on the bookingId+email unique constraint with an unhandled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of the promised BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid) and emailing the address twice.

[BUG] The booking fetch filters only on id and the handler never inspects booking.status, so addGuests treats CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings exactly like confirmed ones. Adding guests to a cancelled booking persists new attendees, runs updateCalendarAttendees against a dead event, and delivers AttendeeScheduledEmail with an ICS marked status CONFIRMED to guests of an event that no longer exists; the BookingListItem menu added in this diff offers 'additional guests' on cancelled rows, inviting exactly this call.

[BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never clears isInvalidEmail, and the Dialog's onOpenChange close path resets neither, so the validation-error state outlives both a successful submission and a dialog close. A user who triggers 'Emails must be unique and valid', fixes the addresses, and adds guests successfully watches the mutation complete with the red error banner still on screen beside the success toast, and reopening the dialog later still shows the stale error.

[BUG] The existing-attendee dedupe compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively, so a case variant of an already-booked email passes the filter named uniqueGuests. Submitting Bob@x.com when bob@x.com already attends creates a second attendee row for the same person, and because that email is in the raw guests list the person also receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation for a booking they already hold.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so the email router's newGuests.includes() treats already-booked attendee emails as new guests. When the submitted list contains an existing attendee's email (the dialog's validation does not block this, and the handler's own dedupe on line 76 anticipates it), that attendee receives AttendeeScheduledEmail — a duplicate full 'you are scheduled' confirmation — instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notification every other existing attendee gets.

[ADVISORY] The email-dispatch failure path discards the caught error object (console.log without err) and the handler still returns { message: "Guests added" }, making guest notification an unobservable best-effort side effect. When the mail provider rejects the batch, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast, the new guests never learn about the booking, and the only production trace is a message-only console.log that cannot identify the cause — operations cannot distinguish a delivered batch from a failed one.

[ADVISORY] The permission gate grants add-guest rights to every attendee of the booking, so the 'guest management' capability is silently handed to the guests themselves rather than scoped to the organizer/team the rest of the gate names. Any booked email that belongs to a cal.com account can call viewer.bookings.addGuests to attach arbitrary addresses to someone else's booking, and each call emails every attendee via sendAddGuestsEmails — an unsolicited mailing path the organizer never sanctioned.

[ADVISORY] The EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials while evt.destinationCalendar points at the organizer's calendar, so whether the calendar event gets updated depends on who invoked the mutation rather than whose booking it is. On the attendee and team-admin paths this same handler authorizes, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently no-ops — the guests appear in Cal.com but never on the organizer's Google/Outlook event, and neither caller nor organizer is told the sync was skipped.

[ADVISORY] The handler inserts plain Attendee rows unconditionally and never branches on booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot (even though it copies seatsPerTimeSlot into evt on line 145), so seat-based event types fall through a guest path designed for ordinary bookings. On a seated event type, addGuests bypasses the seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and creates attendee records the BookingSeat-based seats system does not recognize: a fully-booked seated event accepts unlimited 'guests' who each get a confirmation email while seat counts in the seats UI stay unchanged.

[ADVISORY] The dialog re-declares a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema with a uniqueness refine instead of importing the server's addGuests.schema, and the two copies have already drifted: the server schema carries no uniqueness rule. Guest validation now has two hand-maintained sources (this component and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts); the next rule change (max guest count, email pattern) must be made in both, and missing one leaves the API accepting payloads the UI claims to forbid — drift that is already observable in the server-side duplicate-acceptance finding.
