adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist comparison lowercases only the configured list (line 71) and never the guest string, and the existing-attendee check at line 76 is an exact-case ===, so both guards are case-sensitive. Submitting 'Spam@Example.com' against a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry 'spam@example.com' (or against an attendee stored as 'spam@example.com') bypasses both the blacklist and the duplicate filter, creating and emailing a guest the operator explicitly blocked.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(...toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are never lowercased before checks. The filters use exact string comparisons: duplicate guard `guest === attendee.email` and blacklist guard `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This makes both checks case-sensitive, so inputs like `Spam@Example.com` can bypass a blacklist entry `spam@example.com` and can also bypass duplicate detection against an existing attendee email with different casing, leading to unintended guest creation and emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed from the requesting session user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) rather than the booking organizer's credentials, even though the handler loads booking.user with credentials (include at lines 35-40) and never uses them. On the attendee- or team-admin-initiated paths that the permission gate (lines 46-56) exists to enable, updateCalendarAttendees runs holding the caller's credentials, which lack the organizer's connected Google/Outlook calendar, so new guests never land on the organizer's external event while the mutation still returns 'Guests added' — a silent partial failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches `booking.user` including `credentials` (and `destinationCalendar`) but never uses them. Instead it calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the requesting session user (which may be an attendee or team admin per the permission gate). It then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and returns success regardless of whether the organizer’s external calendar can be updated with the caller’s credentials. This is a concrete mismatch visible in the diff and can lead to incorrect behavior on non-organizer initiated updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw request input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so emails deliberately dropped as already-attendees are still treated as new in email-manager.ts's template selection (newGuests.includes(attendee.email) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail). A user who re-submits a list containing one already-invited email triggers a full 'you are scheduled' AttendeeScheduledEmail to that existing attendee — a duplicate booking confirmation for an event they already hold — instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, guests are filtered into uniqueGuests before updating the booking (so already-attendees are not re-added), but sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is called with the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` (or the actually-added emails). In email-manager.ts, sendAddGuestsEmails uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`; therefore if the request includes an email that was already an attendee, that existing attendee will incorrectly match and receive a full scheduled/confirmation email again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch reuses the validation string 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' for the unrelated condition 'every submitted email is already an attendee or blacklisted'. An organizer re-adding an existing guest sees 'Emails must be unique and valid' over input that is both unique and valid, with no hint the email is already on the booking, so the error is unactionable and the add flow appears broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that are already attendees and those in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. When this filtering results in `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That message (and the corresponding UI string "Emails must be unique and valid") does not match the actual condition (all submitted emails were already on the booking or blacklisted), making the error misleading/unactionable for valid, unique input that simply duplicates existing attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails logs the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards err entirely, while the mutation still returns success. When SMTP or template rendering fails, operators get a log line with no error object, stack, or booking identifier, and the caller sees the 'guests_added' success toast — guests silently receive nothing and the failure cannot be diagnosed from logs.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception (no `err`, stack, bookingId, or user context is logged) and the mutation still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is diff-grounded and creates poor observability/diagnosability for a newly added side-effect (email notification), even if the core mutation (adding attendees + calendar update) succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure (line 56) but never reset — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not the flag, and the dialog stays mounted in BookingListItem so state survives close/reopen. After a single failed attempt, the red 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' banner is still displayed when the user reopens the dialog (same or another booking) over an empty, valid form, and it remains visible after a subsequent successful add — a stale validation error contradicting the visible state.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is only reset on the Cancel button click (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). The `onSuccess` handler resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Since `<AddGuestsDialog ... />` is always rendered in `BookingListItem` (not conditionally unmounted), the dialog component state can persist across close/reopen via `isOpenDialog`, so the red error banner can remain visible after reopening or even after a successful add.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer lookup runs prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0, which throws a raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError (P2025) when booking.userId is null — a state the evt construction itself defends against via booking?.user?. guards (lines 140-144). Any caller who passes the permission gate via the attendee or team path on a booking with an unassigned organizer (nullable userId in the schema) gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx TRPCError, after the booking was already fetched and authorized.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code fetches the organizer via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this will query for `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma “record not found” error) rather than a controlled `TRPCError`. The permission gate earlier allows non-organizers (e.g., `isAttendee`) to proceed, so an attendee on a booking lacking `userId` could hit an unhandled 500 at this organizer lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The booking query filters only on id, with no predicate on status or endTime, so cancelled, rejected, and past bookings are all valid targets for addGuests. Guests (and a CONFIRMED 'REQUEST' ics file) can be attached to a booking the organizer already cancelled, delivering calendar invites that resurrect the cancelled event in every recipient's calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no further guard on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or time window (e.g., `endTime` in the past) before updating attendees and sending emails. The new email templates hardcode an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`), so invoking `addGuests` on an already-cancelled booking would still send a confirmed request/invite and can effectively “resurrect” the event in recipients’ calendars. This behavior is enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dialog hand-duplicates ZAddGuestsInputSchema (z.array(z.string().email()) plus a uniqueness refine) instead of sharing one schema definition with the server's addGuests.schema.ts, and the copies have already drifted — the server schema has no uniqueness refine. Every future change to guest validation (max count, email normalization, format) must be applied in two hand-maintained places; the uniqueness divergence in this very diff is the first instance of client and server enforcing different rules, and the next divergence ships silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate validations that already diverge: the client dialog defines a local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), while the server endpoint input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) only enforces `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. Because the server handler also does not dedupe within the submitted `guests` list (it filters only against existing attendees / blacklist), a caller can submit duplicate emails and potentially create duplicate attendee records / send duplicate notifications, while the UI would block it. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency/validation defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS introduces new operator-facing behavior with no .env.example entry, documentation, or admin surface anywhere in the diff. Self-hosted operators cannot discover the guest blacklist exists, so the guard ships inert in every deployment whose admins don't read handler source; even operators who find it get no documented format contract, which is how the case-sensitivity bypass at lines 74-78 goes unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values are compared without normalization (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). This makes the blacklist check case-sensitive and bypassable by submitting a differently-cased email address. The finding’s broader point that `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is new operator-facing behavior with no corresponding documentation/config surfaced anywhere else in the diff is also supported by the diff (only usage is in the handler).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff ships a 174-line mutation whose entire security posture is the hand-rolled gate at lines 46-56 (admin/owner/organizer/attendee) plus blacklist and dedupe filtering, with no test file touching any of it. The &&-for-|| permission defect in this same gate shipped precisely because no test exercises the team-admin path; the next edit to these lines either locks out a permitted role or opens guest-adding to any logged-in user, with nothing in CI to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission gate computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` using `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` (around the shown lines ~46-56). This requires the caller to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner, which is likely incorrect for an “admin OR owner” authorization check and will lock out legitimate admins (or owners) from adding guests. This is a concrete, diff-visible authorization defect; the lack of any added tests in the diff further supports the reviewer’s concern but is secondary to the actual bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The guest-management dialog seeds MultiEmail with [''] and never fetches or displays the booking's current guests, so the user adds blind. An organizer returning to invite one more guest cannot see who is already on the booking, re-submits an overlapping list, and lands in the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error path — the add flow cannot be completed correctly on a second visit without guessing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AddGuestsDialog` initializes `multiEmailValue` to `[""]` and provides no query/props to fetch or display existing booking attendees (it only receives `bookingId` and calls `trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests`). That makes the UX “blind” when reopening the dialog. However, the finding’s claim that the add flow “cannot be completed correctly on a second visit without guessing” is overstated: the user can still add a single new email without needing the existing list, and the server filters out already-attending emails (`uniqueGuests` in `addGuests.handler.ts`). So this is a real, diff-grounded UX/edge-case concern, not a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner for the team-permission path to grant access. A team ADMIN who is not the owner gets FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') when adding guests to their own team's bookings, and if isTeamAdmin matches only the ADMIN role then even owners fail the team check — the permission path named 'AdminOrOwner' never works for the admin class it was written for, breaking the feature for every non-owner team admin.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner to pass the team-permission path. The subsequent guard `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` means a team admin who is not also the owner will be denied access, contradicting the variable name/intended logic (admin OR owner).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, so the two copies of the same validation already disagree in this diff. Any caller other than this dialog (direct tRPC mutation, API client, or a stale bundle) sending guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation, and createMany inserts two identical Attendee rows for one person, who then receives duplicate emails and appears twice in the calendar event; the client-side guard was the only thing preventing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different validations for the same input: client-side `AddGuestsDialog` defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness, but server-side `packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts` only uses `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing booking attendees and blacklisted emails, but does not dedupe duplicates within the `guests` input itself, so `guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` can reach `createMany` and create duplicate attendee rows (and then `attendeesList`/calendar event can include duplicates). This is a correctness defect exposed by the diff because the server trusts potentially duplicated input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() bound, and the handler fans each guest out into a DB row, a confirmation email, and calendar/ICS updates. Any permitted caller — including a mere attendee of any booking, since isAttendee grants access — can submit thousands of emails in a single mutation, forcing an unbounded createMany plus an unbounded email and external calendar fan-out on one request with no rate or count limit anywhere in the path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` with `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defined as `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`/size limit) and the handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) uses `createMany` to insert one attendee row per guest (`attendees.createMany.data = guestsFullDetails`). It then performs additional per-attendee fan-out work: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends an email for each attendee. Access control explicitly allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to execute this mutation. Nothing in the diff shows rate limiting or count limiting, so a permitted caller can submit a very large `guests` array and trigger unbounded DB writes and email/calendar side effects in a single request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate check reads booking.attendees (lines 74-78) and then inserts in a separate update with no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email) — a check-then-insert TOCTOU with nothing backing it at the schema level. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking and the same email both pass the filter and both execute createMany, producing duplicate Attendee rows that no constraint forbids; the same missing invariant also lets any other write path create the same duplicate.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees) then filters `uniqueGuests` using `booking.attendees` and later performs a separate `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`. This is a classic non-atomic check-then-write flow, so concurrent `addGuests` calls could bypass the in-memory duplicate filter and race at insert time. However, the finding’s claim that there is “no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email)” and that duplicates are therefore definitely insertable is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/DB constraints shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dedup filter compares raw guest strings with exact equality (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist in the same expression lowercases its entries — normalization is applied asymmetrically within one filter. Resubmitting an already-attendee email in different casing (John@X.com vs stored john@x.com) slips past the duplicate filter and creates a second Attendee row for the same person (duplicate emails, double calendar invite); the same asymmetry means the lowercased blacklist never matches a mixed-case guest string.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but only the blacklist is lowercased (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`). Since `guest` is not normalized (and `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `.email()` without lowercasing), a mixed-case resubmission like `John@X.com` can bypass both the duplicate-attendee check (if stored as `john@x.com`) and the blacklist check, resulting in `createMany` inserting a second attendee row and triggering extra calendar/email updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] organizer is fetched with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }) while Booking.userId is nullable, and the permission gate above explicitly lets plain attendees reach this line. For any booking with a null userId, an attendee who passes the isAttendee check hits findFirstOrThrow on id 0, which throws an unhandled PrismaClientNotFoundError — the client gets a raw 500 instead of a clean error, after already being told they had permission.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission gate allows attendees through (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...)` and the subsequent `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`). Immediately after, organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined (the code itself anticipates this via `|| 0`), an authorized attendee will hit a `findFirstOrThrow` on `id: 0`, which will throw and surface as an unhandled server error instead of a controlled TRPC error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler validates only caller identity — never booking.status or booking times — before creating attendees and dispatching CONFIRMED invitations, and BookingListItem adds the 'additional_guests' menu item unconditionally for every booking row. Guests can be added to CANCELLED and past bookings; the new guests then receive a full booking-confirmation email with a status:CONFIRMED ICS for an event that no longer exists, and the cancelled booking's attendee list is permanently mutated.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched and permission-checked, but there is no validation of booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled) or time bounds (past events) before mutating `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and then sending emails/invites. The email templates created here (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` will dispatch these for all attendees regardless of booking status. On the UI side, `BookingListItem` adds the `additional_guests` action unconditionally to `bookingActions` (no checks for cancelled/past), so users can trigger this flow for any listed booking row, including ones that should not accept modifications. This can permanently mutate attendees for non-active bookings and send misleading CONFIRMED invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] EventManager is constructed from the requesting user (ctx.user) and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), but evt.destinationCalendar belongs to the booking's organizer (booking.user), so the credentials never match the calendar being updated when requester != organizer. When a non-organizer (an attendee or team admin — exactly the callers the permission model allows) adds guests, the EventManager holds the requester's credentials, finds no credential for the organizer's destination calendar, and the external Google/Outlook calendar event is silently left without the new attendees while the mutation returns 'Guests added'.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` and `credentials` come from the requesting user (`ctx.user` / `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). However, the event’s destination calendar is derived from the booking/organizer side (`evt.destinationCalendar` uses `booking.destinationCalendar` or `booking.user.destinationCalendar`). Since the permission model allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to call this mutation, the EventManager may not have credentials matching the organizer’s destination calendar, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` can fail to update the external calendar when requester != organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isAttendee permission check compares attendee.email === user.email with exact case-sensitive string equality, though attendee emails are stored exactly as typed at booking time. A user whose account email casing differs from the mixed-case email they booked with (attendee rows are not normalized) is denied with FORBIDDEN even though they are a legitimate attendee of the booking, while the same email matched case-insensitively elsewhere in the codebase.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler` the permission check for attendees is `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)` (case-sensitive). Since this handler gates access with `FORBIDDEN` when `isAttendee` is false, any mismatch in email casing between the stored attendee row and the session `user.email` would incorrectly deny a legitimate attendee from adding guests. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) on either side in this comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input list instead of uniqueGuests, so emails that were filtered out of creation still drive the new-guest classification (newGuests.includes) in email-manager. An existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (filtered from creation) matches newGuests.includes(attendee.email) and receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail 'your booking is confirmed' email again instead of the 'new guests added' notice — a duplicate re-confirmation for someone who was not re-added.
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same misclassification bug in sendAddGuestsEmails: it iterates over the full calendarEvent.attendees list but decides email type by checking newGuests.includes(attendee.email), where newGuests comes from the raw input guests list (not the truly-added/unique set). This can cause existing attendees whose email appears in the input to be treated as "new" and receive the wrong email (e.g., re-confirmation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The mutation is non-idempotent and its error vocabulary conflates 'no new emails' with 'invalid emails': when every submitted email already exists on the booking, uniqueGuests is empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. After any post-commit failure (the uncaught updateCalendarAttendees throw at line 165, or a client timeout) the guests are already persisted but the user sees an error; clicking Add again deterministically returns 'emails must be unique and valid' for emails that were valid and were in fact already added, so the user is told their correct input is invalid while the operation actually succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB update (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) happens before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and before the email send. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a `try/catch`, any throw there will cause the mutation to return an error after guests have already been persisted. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out already-existing attendees; if all submitted emails were already added, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which misrepresents the situation as invalid input even though the emails are valid and the prior attempt may have succeeded in persisting them. This matches the finding’s idempotency/UX error-vocabulary concern and is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails loops over calendarEvent.team.members, but its only caller (addGuestsHandler) builds the CalendarEvent literal without any team property, so this branch can never execute in the new flow. Team members of team bookings are silently never notified when guests are added — the loop is dead code that will mislead the next maintainer into believing team notifications happen; either populate evt.team in the handler or delete the branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts) there is an explicit branch to notify `calendarEvent.team.members`, but the only new caller shown (`addGuestsHandler` in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts) constructs `evt: CalendarEvent` without any `team` property at all. Given the optional chaining (`calendarEvent.team?.members`), that loop will never run in this flow, so team-member notifications implied by the code are not actually sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "" and then receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail confirmation template via the newGuests classification in email-manager. Every newly added guest's confirmation email (and the ICS attendee entry) greets a blank name — 'Hi ,' with no recipient name — on every single add-guests call, since there is no fallback (e.g. email local part) anywhere in the path.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are persisted with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails`), and the email payload attendees are built from the DB attendee records without any fallback (`name: attendee.name`). `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` then sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to addresses present in `newGuests` (the input `guests` array), meaning newly added guests will receive the standard scheduled template while having an empty `attendee.name` value in the `CalendarEvent` used for rendering. The diff shows no fallback name being set anywhere in this new add-guests path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees into evt, showing seat-based event types are in scope, but never enforces seat capacity and creates plain Attendee rows with no BookingSeat records. An organizer of a seats event adds unlimited guests past seatsPerTimeSlot with no check, and those guests bypass BookingSeat-based capacity and seat-cancellation accounting while still inflating attendee lists used by emails and ICS — the seat invariant the schema elsewhere maintains is unenforced on this new write path.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (even though that field is carried into `evt`). This creates a write path that can increase attendee count beyond any seat capacity implied by `seatsPerTimeSlot`, and there is no seat-specific persistence/guarding logic shown (it never checks remaining capacity before adding).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||, so it is true only for users who are simultaneously team admin and team owner, silently inverting the OR that the variable's own name declares. A team admin who is not also the team owner (and a team owner without a separate admin membership) calling viewer.bookings.addGuests on a team booking is rejected with FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, so the intended 'admin or owner may manage guests' permission path is dead code — and the diff ships no test that would have caught it.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore reject team admins who aren’t also owners (and owners who aren’t also admins), contradicting the variable name and typical intended logic (`admin || owner`). No tests are added in the diff to cover these roles for `viewer.bookings.addGuests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71 but the guest value is compared unnormalized on line 77, so blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) never matches a mixed-case submission. An operator who sets BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=user@example.com watches User@Example.com pass the filter, get persisted as a booking attendee, and receive the event email — the abuse-prevention control is defeated by any case variation.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is not lowercased. This makes blacklist matching case-sensitive and allows mixed-case emails (e.g., `User@Example.com`) to bypass a lowercase blacklist entry and be persisted/sent emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees and the blacklist and never dedupes within the input guests array, so the uniqueness invariant the feature promises is enforced only by the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog. A direct viewer.bookings.addGuests mutation with ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the handler and reaches prisma createMany on line 101, persisting two identical attendee rows (or aborting on the bookingId+email unique constraint with an unhandled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of the promised BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid) and emailing the address twice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and those in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (via `guests.filter(...)`), but it does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. The server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also lacks a uniqueness refinement (it only validates `.email()`). Therefore a direct `viewer.bookings.addGuests` call with duplicate emails (e.g. `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`) will pass server validation and flow into `createMany` with duplicate rows. This can lead to duplicate attendee records and/or a DB constraint error, and it can also result in duplicate emails because `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and would send per attendee entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking fetch filters only on id and the handler never inspects booking.status, so addGuests treats CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings exactly like confirmed ones. Adding guests to a cancelled booking persists new attendees, runs updateCalendarAttendees against a dead event, and delivers AttendeeScheduledEmail with an ICS marked status CONFIRMED to guests of an event that no longer exists; the BookingListItem menu added in this diff offers 'additional guests' on cancelled rows, inviting exactly this call.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no subsequent guard on any booking lifecycle/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before mutating attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sending emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). Separately, the UI adds the `additional_guests` action unconditionally to `BookingListItem`’s menu (no status-based filtering shown), so cancelled rows would still offer this action. If bookings can be CANCELLED/REJECTED in the model, this diff would allow adding guests and sending CONFIRMED ICS/email updates for non-active bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never clears isInvalidEmail, and the Dialog's onOpenChange close path resets neither, so the validation-error state outlives both a successful submission and a dialog close. A user who triggers 'Emails must be unique and valid', fixes the addresses, and adds guests successfully watches the mutation complete with the red error banner still on screen beside the success toast, and reopening the dialog later still shows the stale error.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure (`handleAdd`), but it is never reset on successful mutation: `onSuccess` only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])` (no `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Also, the dialog close path via `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>` will toggle `isOpenDialog` without clearing `isInvalidEmail` or `multiEmailValue`, so closing/reopening the dialog can retain the stale error banner. Only the explicit Cancel button clears `isInvalidEmail`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The existing-attendee dedupe compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively, so a case variant of an already-booked email passes the filter named uniqueGuests. Submitting Bob@x.com when bob@x.com already attends creates a second attendee row for the same person, and because that email is in the raw guests list the person also receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation for a booking they already hold.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe/filter for existing attendees is case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since inputs are not normalized (no `.toLowerCase()`), `Bob@x.com` will not match an existing `bob@x.com`, so `uniqueGuests` will include it and `createMany` will insert a duplicate attendee row for the same mailbox. Also, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw `guests` list (not `uniqueGuests`), and `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive), so a case-variant can cause the same real recipient to get a “scheduled” email for the newly-added duplicate address even if they were already an attendee (delivered to the same inbox in practice).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so the email router's newGuests.includes() treats already-booked attendee emails as new guests. When the submitted list contains an existing attendee's email (the dialog's validation does not block this, and the handler's own dedupe on line 76 anticipates it), that attendee receives AttendeeScheduledEmail — a duplicate full 'you are scheduled' confirmation — instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notification every other existing attendee gets.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted) and only persists those via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check controls whether an attendee receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the user submitted an email that was already an attendee, that email can still be in the raw `guests` list, causing an existing attendee to be treated as “new” and receive a duplicate scheduled email. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The email-dispatch failure path discards the caught error object (console.log without err) and the handler still returns { message: "Guests added" }, making guest notification an unobservable best-effort side effect. When the mail provider rejects the batch, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast, the new guests never learn about the booking, and the only production trace is a message-only console.log that cannot identify the cause — operations cannot distinguish a delivered batch from a failed one.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try/catch` that logs only a generic message (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`) and swallows the exception, then the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This makes email notification a best-effort side effect with poor observability and no way for the caller/UI to distinguish a successful guest-add from a guest-add where notifications failed, as the caught error object isn’t logged or propagated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The permission gate grants add-guest rights to every attendee of the booking, so the 'guest management' capability is silently handed to the guests themselves rather than scoped to the organizer/team the rest of the gate names. Any booked email that belongs to a cal.com account can call viewer.bookings.addGuests to attach arbitrary addresses to someone else's booking, and each call emails every attendee via sendAddGuestsEmails — an unsolicited mailing path the organizer never sanctioned.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly allows any authenticated user whose email matches an existing booking attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the gate only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` (in `addGuests.handler.ts`). This means a booking attendee with a cal.com account can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests` for that booking and attach arbitrary addresses. The handler then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` broadcasts emails to the organizer/team and to *all* attendees (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), creating an unsolicited mailing path initiated by an attendee rather than the organizer/team.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials while evt.destinationCalendar points at the organizer's calendar, so whether the calendar event gets updated depends on who invoked the mutation rather than whose booking it is. On the attendee and team-admin paths this same handler authorizes, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently no-ops — the guests appear in Cal.com but never on the organizer's Google/Outlook event, and neither caller nor organizer is told the sync was skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows non-organizers to call it (`isAttendee` / `isTeamAdminOrOwner`), but it builds the `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and spreads `...user` (the caller) into the manager. Meanwhile the calendar target is derived from the booking/organizer context (`evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` or `booking.user.destinationCalendar`). This mismatch means an attendee/team member invoking the mutation may not have credentials that can update the organizer’s connected destination calendar, so the external calendar attendee update can fail to apply even though Cal.com attendees are updated in Prisma.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler inserts plain Attendee rows unconditionally and never branches on booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot (even though it copies seatsPerTimeSlot into evt on line 145), so seat-based event types fall through a guest path designed for ordinary bookings. On a seated event type, addGuests bypasses the seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and creates attendee records the BookingSeat-based seats system does not recognize: a fully-booked seated event accepts unlimited 'guests' who each get a confirmation email while seat counts in the seats UI stay unchanged.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation always appends to booking.attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) and never checks booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot or any capacity/seat allocation before adding guests, even though it forwards seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into the CalendarEvent (evt). The diff does not show how seated bookings are enforced/stored elsewhere, so the stronger claims about a separate BookingSeat system/UI not recognizing these rows aren’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the missing seats/capacity handling for seat-based event types is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dialog re-declares a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema with a uniqueness refine instead of importing the server's addGuests.schema, and the two copies have already drifted: the server schema carries no uniqueness rule. Guest validation now has two hand-maintained sources (this component and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts); the next rule change (max guest count, email pattern) must be made in both, and missing one leaves the API accepting payloads the UI claims to forbid — drift that is already observable in the server-side duplicate-acceptance finding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate validation schemas: the client dialog defines a local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx), while the server TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only checks `{ bookingId: number, guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness rule (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). This is clear schema duplication and drift risk. The server handler also doesn’t dedupe duplicate emails within the `guests` array (it only filters against existing attendees/blacklist), so the API can accept inputs the UI forbids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "" and nothing in the flow ever backfills a name, so every downstream render of attendee.name for an added guest is blank. The confirmation email a new guest receives renders blanks wherever the template prints the attendee name, and the ICS/calendar update the organizer receives lists an attendee with no CN, leaving added guests indistinguishable from each other in any UI that shows attendee names.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are persisted with `name: ""` (`guestsFullDetails`), and that value is then used to build `evt.attendees` (from `bookingAttendees.attendees`). Nothing in this diff backfills or derives a name later. As a result, new guests will have blank `attendee.name` in the `CalendarEvent` used for `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and for the emails sent via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, so any downstream rendering that expects a non-empty attendee name (email templates / calendar attendee CN) will be blank for added guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is a brand-new operator control whose only existence proof is this env read — the diff adds no .env.example entry, documentation, or admin surface for it. Operators cannot discover that guest-email blacklisting exists, so it ships inert: deployments that need to block abusive domains run with an empty list, and those who do find the variable discover its enforcement is the case-sensitive compare flagged separately in this review.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new operational control `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` in `addGuests.handler.ts` (splitting/lowercasing it into `blacklistedGuestEmails`) but the PR diff shows no corresponding documentation, `.env.example` update, or any other discoverable surface indicating this configuration exists. That makes the review point about operator discoverability/delivery completeness diff-grounded, but it’s not a directly verifiable runtime defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest emails compared against them at line 77 are not normalized, so `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` fails to match case-variant addresses. An operator who sets BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=blocked@example.com to stop a specific address from being contacted (compliance/opt-out blocklist) is trivially bypassed by submitting "Blocked@Example.com" — the address passes the filter, is written as a BookingAttendee, and is emailed the full booking details (description, location, video call URL and password), defeating the control the env var exists to provide; the same missing normalization also lets a caller re-add an existing attendee under a case variant.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is not lowercased. Since emails are case-variant strings, a user can bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=blocked@example.com` by submitting `Blocked@Example.com`, which will not match the lowercase blocklist and will be persisted/emailed. The same lack of normalization exists in the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email`, allowing re-adding an existing attendee via case variants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an unbounded, non-unique array (`z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` and no uniqueness refinement), so the uniqueness/validity enforcement in AddGuestsDialog's local refine is client-only. Any authenticated user who is organizer/attendee of a booking can call viewer.bookings.addGuests directly with a payload of thousands of emails (duplicates included) in one request, creating thousands of BookingAttendee rows in a single createMany and triggering a matching number of emails (plus re-emails of every existing attendee) from the platform's sending domain — a mailbombing and DB-flooding primitive the dialog deliberately prevents, and a duplicate of the same victim email re-sends the booking email repeatedly.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows server-side input validation for `viewer.bookings.addGuests` is only `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`, no uniqueness). The handler also does not dedupe within the request: `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` only filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, not duplicates in `guests` itself, and then `createMany` writes them (`attendees.createMany.data = guestsFullDetails`). It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original (possibly huge/duplicate) array, and email sending iterates `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, so if duplicates were inserted into `attendees`, multiple emails could be sent to the same address. This enables an authenticated organizer/attendee to submit an arbitrarily large list directly to the mutation, creating DB load and triggering mass email sends from the platform domain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isTeamAdminOrOwner authorization check joins the two role queries with `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the caller to be both team admin and team owner when the variable name and intent are either-or. A team ADMIN who is not the OWNER is rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings (and depending on isTeamAdmin's role matching, even owners can fail both prongs), so the authorization check does not implement its stated policy — fail-closed, so no exposure, but the feature is silently broken for a whole role and the next editor who 'fixes' the operator to `||` will be changing live authorization logic without any test having pinned the intended semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be both admin and owner. Given the variable name and subsequent authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, a team admin (but not owner) will be incorrectly rejected with `FORBIDDEN` when adding guests to team bookings. This is a concrete behavior defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the error object entirely, logs only the constant string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails", and the handler then unconditionally returns success. When email delivery fails, the new attendee rows are already committed and every caller sees the 'Guests added' success toast while the new guests never receive their invitations; operators get no stack, no error code, and no message to diagnose the failure, turning a mail-provider outage into silent data divergence between the calendar/DB and the notified participants.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that (a) ignores the caught `err` and logs only a constant string (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`), and (b) does not rethrow or otherwise signal failure, so the handler proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }` regardless. Since the DB update (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) happens before the email send, an email-provider failure yields a committed guest list but a successful response/"guests_added" toast with no diagnostic error detail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Attendee authorization is granted purely on `attendee.email === user.email` string equality, making possession of an account whose primary email string matches an attendee the credential for modifying that booking. Anyone who can register a session on an account whose email equals a booking attendee's email gains add-guests rights on every booking that address attended — including the ability to export full booking details (description, location, video call URL and password) to arbitrary email addresses of their choosing via the guest emails — and because bookingId is a bare sequential integer, target bookings are discoverable by probing for FORBIDDEN-vs-success; the check trusts the email claim rather than any booking-scoped grant.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any authenticated user whose `user.email` matches any existing attendee email (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). This makes email-string membership the sole booking-scoped credential for attendees to call `addGuests`, which then (a) updates attendees in DB and (b) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, propagating full event details (incl. `location` and `videoCallData` with URL/password when present) to arbitrary `guests` emails. The endpoint also takes a bare numeric `bookingId` (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`), which supports enumeration/probing patterns even though sequentiality isn’t proven in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The uniqueGuests filter only strips emails that already exist as booking attendees or are blacklisted, so duplicate emails within a single request pass the router's ZAddGuestsInputSchema (which has no uniqueness refine, unlike the dialog's private copy) and reach createMany at line 101, inserting two attendee rows with the same email. Any caller of viewer.bookings.addGuests that bypasses AddGuestsDialog's client-side refine (another client, a stale bundle, a direct tRPC call) submits ['dup@x.com','dup@x.com'] and gets duplicate BookingAttendee rows — the guest appears twice in the attendee list and receives the notification twice — while the 'emails must be unique' invariant that the handler's own BAD_REQUEST message (line 81) promises is enforced only in the browser; a dialog-level test of the client schema would pass green while the API violates the contract.
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: uniqueGuests only filters out existing/blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming request, allowing repeated emails to reach createMany and insert duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The try/catch around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows every email failure and discards the caught err entirely (console.log prints the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without it), after which the handler returns {message: 'Guests added'} as success. When the mail provider or a template render fails during add-guests, the organizer sees the 'Guests added' success toast while no guest is ever notified, the error object is lost so operations cannot diagnose the outage, and the mutation's success return is structurally decoupled from the email side effect — a handler test running against a throwing email mock passes green, so no test can ever detect email-delivery regressions through this endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to return success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This means email delivery failures won’t be surfaced to the client and the caught `err` isn’t logged, reducing diagnosability/observability. However, the primary mutation work (persisting attendees and updating calendar attendees) still succeeds, so this is more an error-handling/UX/ops concern than a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input instead of the uniqueGuests list that was actually added, so the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) branch in email-manager.ts misclassifies pre-existing attendees as newly added. A user who includes an already-booked attendee's email alongside a new one — which the dialog permits, since its refine only checks uniqueness within the entered list, never against existing attendees — causes that existing attendee to receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail 'your event has been scheduled' re-confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests were added' notice that the else-branch in sendAddGuestsEmails was written to deliver.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters the input to `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only adds those via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide who gets the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the caller includes an email already on the booking (allowed by the dialog’s client-side `refine`, which only checks duplicates within the entered list), that pre-existing attendee email is still present in `guests`, so they are misclassified as “new” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` even though they weren’t newly added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dialog hand-maintains a private ZAddGuestsInputSchema (a bare email array with a uniqueness refine) alongside the router's identically-named ZAddGuestsInputSchema (an object with bookingId and no refine) in addGuests.schema.ts — two divergent copies of one contract shipped in the same PR. The copies already disagree in this diff (the client enforces uniqueness, the server does not), so the next engineer tightening email rules updates one schema and not the other, and any test importing 'the schema' validates against whichever copy it happens to reach rather than the contract the API actually enforces; deleting the inline schema and importing a single shared definition removes a place-to-update and one of the two validation paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different schemas with the same conceptual purpose/name: the UI dialog defines an inline `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx), while the API router imports `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` from `addGuests.schema.ts` as an object `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness rule (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts and _router.tsx). This is a real, diff-grounded contract duplication/divergence risk (client validation differs from server validation), but it’s not directly a guaranteed runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fallback in showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error") is unreachable because message is a template literal that is non-empty on every code path. The 'unable_to_add_guests' string added to common.json in this same diff can never be displayed to anyone, and a failure with no err.data (network-level error) renders the literal toast 'undefined: <raw message>' — users hit by an error see a code-prefixed raw string or 'undefined: undefined' instead of the human-readable message the new key was added to provide.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Because `message` is always a (non-empty) string due to being a template literal, the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never be used. If `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g., network/unknown error shape), the toast can become `"undefined: ..."`, which matches the finding and makes the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation effectively dead code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never clears isInvalidEmail, and handleAdd never clears it on successful re-validation either, so the flag set at line 56 persists across successful adds. After one invalid attempt, the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error stays visible through the subsequent successful add, and because the component stays mounted in BookingListItem with only the open state toggling, the next time the user opens the dialog a fresh empty form appears with a phantom validation error already showing.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed `safeParse` (handleAdd) but is never reset on successful validation or in the mutation `onSuccess`. `onSuccess` only does `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])`, so because the component remains mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and only `open` toggles), reopening the dialog can show the error block (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) even with a fresh/empty form. The Cancel button clears it, but success path does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] addGuestsHandler commits the new guests to Postgres via prisma.booking.update/attendees.createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar sync at line 165 runs, with no compensation for a calendar-side failure. A throw from eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (expired token, deleted external event, API error) leaves the guests already persisted in the DB, absent from the organizer's calendar, and the notification emails never sent because sendAddGuestsEmails is downstream; the mutation returns an error while the data was written, and every retry with the same emails is rejected because the dedupe filter at lines 74-78 now sees them as existing attendees and throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — with no removeGuests mutation in the router, the DB/calendar divergence is permanent and only fixable by direct DB intervention.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees to Postgres first (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`, lines ~92-106), then performs the external calendar update (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, line ~165) with no transaction or compensation/rollback. Because `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch, any throw there will cause the mutation to error after the DB write has already succeeded, preventing the downstream `sendAddGuestsEmails` call and leaving DB/calendar out of sync. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server schema (guests: z.array(z.string().email()), lines 3-6) omits the uniqueness refinement its client twin applies (AddGuestsDialog.tsx lines 28-31), and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-78) only removes duplicates against already-stored attendees, never within the input array itself. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the client-side dialog enforces unique emails via a zod `.refine` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) but the server input schema only validates email format (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts) and the handler’s `uniqueGuests` filter only excludes emails already present on the booking and blacklisted ones (addGuests.handler.ts), not duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guests array has no .max() length bound (line 5), so a single authorized request can bulk-insert an unbounded number of attendee rows. Any authed attendee (the isAttendee path grants this to a mere participant) can submit hundreds of emails in one call: createMany writes hundreds of junk Attendee rows onto someone else's booking and sendAddGuestsEmails fires one email per attendee per request, turning a single mutation into a mass-mail/spam blast that pollutes the booking permanently since no removal path exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`/rate limiting) in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and the handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to invoke it. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dedupe filter compares guest emails to stored attendee emails with case-sensitive === (line 76), and neither zod's .email() nor the filter normalizes case, so a case-variant of an already-added attendee ('Guest@Example.com' vs stored 'guest@example.com') passes as unique. createMany persists a second Attendee row for the same person, who then appears twice in the booking's attendee list, receives two separate emails, and is listed twice in the calendar event ICS — the uniqueness invariant this endpoint exists to enforce is broken by ordinary mixed-case typing.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe logic uses strict, case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`) when filtering out already-existing attendees, and neither the Zod schema (`z.string().email()`) nor the handler normalizes emails (e.g., `toLowerCase()`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist lowercases its configured entries (line 71) but compares them against non-lowercased guest input (line 77), so no mixed-case spelling of a blacklisted address can ever match. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The createMany persists guest attendee rows with name: "" and the organizer's timeZone and locale (lines 83-90), bypassing the attendee validation the normal booking flow applies, and no update path exists anywhere in the router to repair these rows. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw request input (guests, line 168) instead of the actually-persisted uniqueGuests, so the email dispatch in email-manager.ts (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) classifies any input email matching an existing attendee as a brand-new guest. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters the request `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing booking attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists `uniqueGuests`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array. If the request re-submits an already-existing attendee email alongside new ones, that existing attendee email is still in `guests` and will match `includes`, causing that attendee to receive the full scheduled/invite email again even though they were not newly added.
