adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails logs the constant string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards the caught err object (lines 169-171). When guest emails fail in production, operators get a bare one-line log with no stack, no cause, and no monitoring signal while the API returns success — organizer and guests silently receive nothing and triage requires blind reproduction.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` (near the end). The caught `err` is not logged/propagated, and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so email delivery failures become silent (no stack/cause, no signal) while the mutation succeeds. This is a concrete, diff-grounded operational/observability issue rather than a strictly verifiable correctness bug in the primary DB update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The team-permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && (lines 46-48) although the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner and the intent is either role. Since an owner is always also an admin, the check degenerates to owners-only: team admins who are not owners are rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their own team's bookings, breaking the feature for the entire admin role.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the user to be both admin and owner, contradicting the variable name and the likely intended permission of “admin OR owner”. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail the permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, blocking them from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the error entirely (a console.log of a static string with the err object never logged) and the handler returns success 'Guests added' regardless. When the email step fails (SMTP outage, template error), the guests are persisted to the booking and calendar but never receive any notification, the organizer sees the success toast 'Guests added', and the swallowed err leaves zero diagnostic trace — the API reports success while the notification work was dropped.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email notification step is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the function then unconditionally returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means any SMTP/template failure is silently ignored (the caught `err` is not logged or rethrown), while the mutation still resolves successfully and the UI shows the success toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`). The diff therefore introduces behavior where notifications can fail with no actionable diagnostics and no API-level indication of failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Attendees are committed by prisma.booking.update (lines 92-106) before the completely unguarded eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call, with no rollback, compensation, or error mapping between the committed write and the remote calendar step. If the calendar step throws (expired/revoked OAuth credential, provider error), the mutation rejects with a raw INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR while the guest rows are already persisted; the user retries and uniqueGuests is now empty, so the retry fails with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — the booking is left with guests that are not on the organizer's calendar and no working path to complete the operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write is committed via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`, and that calendar update is not wrapped in any error handling/compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., revoked credentials/provider failure), the mutation will reject after persisting the new attendee rows. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees`, so it can become empty and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), leaving guests persisted but not synced to the calendar with no clear recovery path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner joins the two role checks with && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both team admin and team owner despite the variable's 'Or' name. A caller who is a team admin but not the team owner fails the right-hand predicate and receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking (unless they are also the organizer or an attendee) — exactly the access this check was written to grant; if isTeamAdmin does not count OWNER memberships, owners are denied too and the team path is dead for everyone.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the new permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` and stored in a variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. This requires the user to be both an admin and an owner to pass the team permission path. The subsequent check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` means a user who is only a team admin (or only a team owner) will be denied unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, which contradicts the intended “admin OR owner” access suggested by the variable name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() cap and no .min(1), leaving the request payload unbounded on an authenticated mutation path. One request with a 10,000-entry array passes validation: createMany writes 10,000 BookingAttendee rows and sendAddGuestsEmails dispatches one email per resulting attendee plus the organizer copy — unbounded storage writes and SMTP fan-out with no cap anywhere on the path, and each subsequent addGuests call compounds the attendee count the email loop iterates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an authenticated `addGuests` mutation whose input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)` or `.max(...)` cap (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts). The handler then `createMany` inserts one attendee row per provided email (addGuests.handler.ts: `attendees.createMany` from `uniqueGuests`) and then builds `evt.attendees` from *all* booking attendees and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends an email per attendee plus organizer/team copies (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). There is no bound anywhere in this path, so a large array (e.g., 10k) would pass validation and trigger unbounded DB writes and email fan-out, and subsequent calls increase `calendarEvent.attendees` size, compounding the loop cost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the permission block explicitly admits attendees and team admins, while the booking query fetches booking.user's credentials (lines 34-40) and never uses them. When a non-organizer adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's credentials, which do not include the organizer's connected calendar, so the organizer's Google/Outlook event silently never gains the new attendees — and the handler discards updateCalendarAttendees' return value, so the desync between Cal.com attendees and the real calendar event is reported nowhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` / `isAttendee` checks), but the calendar sync is performed via `EventManager` constructed with the *calling* user’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. At the same time, the booking fetch includes `booking.user.credentials` (and `booking.user.destinationCalendar`) but those credentials are never used. This creates a concrete risk that when someone other than the organizer invokes the mutation, `updateCalendarAttendees` runs without the organizer’s connected calendar credentials and cannot update the organizer’s external calendar event, causing Cal.com attendees to diverge from the real calendar event with no handling/validation in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate-guest and blacklist filters compare emails case-sensitively: guest === attendee.email, and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) tests an un-lowercased guest against a lowercased list. Submitting 'John@Example.com' when 'john@example.com' already attends bypasses the dedup and creates a second attendee row for the same person (who then receives both a guests-added email and a duplicate scheduled email), and any uppercase variant of a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry bypasses the blacklist entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with case-sensitive comparisons: it filters out existing attendees via `guest === attendee.email` and filters blacklisted emails via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is explicitly lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) while `guest` is not, so case variants bypass the blacklist. Likewise, case variants of an existing attendee email are not deduped and will be inserted via `attendees.createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows for the same email differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests instead of uniqueGuests, so the newGuests.includes() branch in email-manager classifies emails that were filtered out of the database write as new guests. If the submitted list contains an already-attending email alongside a new one, that existing attendee matches newGuests and receives a duplicate full AttendeeScheduledEmail ('You are scheduled') instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail guests-added notice the flow intends for existing attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write uses `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails) via `createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }`, but the email send call uses the unfiltered `guests` (`await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`). In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which template to send per attendee by checking `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Because `newGuests` is the raw input list, an email that was already an attendee but included in the submitted `guests` array will be misclassified as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again instead of the intended guests-added notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The toast fallback `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` is dead code because the template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy. The user-friendly fallback can never render: every failure shows a raw error-code prefix plus whatever err.message contains (e.g. 'BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid', or untranslated internal text when the message is not a translation key), misdirecting the user instead of showing 'Unable to add guests'.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (e.g., even `undefined: `), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback. This makes the intended user-friendly fallback unreachable and can surface raw/untranslated internal error keys instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. After any validation failure followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows an empty form together with the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner — telling the user their empty input is invalid — and the only path that clears the flag is Cancel, not a successful operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd` -> `setIsInvalidEmail(true)`), but the `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess` handler only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` and does **not** reset `isInvalidEmail`. The error banner is rendered solely based on `isInvalidEmail` (`{isInvalidEmail && (...)}`), so after a failed attempt followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog will still show the error banner even though the form was cleared. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer lookup uses prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with where id: booking.userId || 0 — an unguarded throw on a nullable booking.userId. For a booking whose userId is null (orphaned on user deletion — the || 0 fallback shows null is anticipated), a caller who passes the permission check via isAttendee reaches findFirstOrThrow with id 0, which throws Prisma's P2025 NotFoundError and surfaces as a raw 500 instead of the 4xx every surrounding failure path in this handler returns.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` fallback indicates `booking.userId` may be null/undefined. A caller can still pass the permission gate as an attendee (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...)`) even when `booking.userId` is null, and then `findFirstOrThrow` will run with `id: 0`, triggering Prisma's not-found throw. This throw is not caught and will surface as an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 4xx like the rest of the handler's error paths (`TRPCError` for NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN/BAD_REQUEST).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] bookingId is z.number() with no .int() or positive bound, so fractional and out-of-range ids pass input validation and reach Prisma's Int column. A client sending bookingId 1.5 passes the tRPC input check, and Prisma throws PrismaClientValidationError ('Expected Int, provided Float') that surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR 500 instead of the 400 the input contract should return.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `bookingId` is validated as `z.number()` with no `.int()`/positive constraint. That allows fractional values like `1.5` to pass tRPC validation, and `addGuests.handler.ts` then uses it directly in Prisma queries (`where: { id: bookingId }`). Since `booking.id` is an Int column, Prisma will reject floats at runtime (PrismaClientValidationError), which would surface as a 500 rather than a 400 input-validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] replyTo is built by spreading every attendee email with no bound, and the addGuests flow grows the attendee list on every invocation. Each addGuests call lengthens the organizer email's reply-to header; with a large guest list it carries hundreds or thousands of addresses that receiving MTAs reject or truncate, so the one message meant to tell the organizer that guests were added fails and disappears into the handler's swallowing catch — while every attendee's address is exposed to every recipient of that copy.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the organizer email sets `replyTo` to `[this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, i.e., it includes every attendee email with no bound. The new `addGuests` flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`) appends attendees on each call (`attendees.createMany`), so the attendee list (and thus `replyTo`) can grow unbounded over repeated additions. This can both (a) leak all attendee emails to every recipient of the organizer copy (organizer/team members) via the Reply-To header, and (b) cause oversized headers that MTAs may reject/truncate. Additionally, the handler wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails` in a broad `try/catch` that only logs and continues, so an email delivery failure would be silently swallowed as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking fetch has no status filter and the handler never checks booking.status before adding guests. Adding guests to a cancelled or rejected booking (the menu item is rendered on every list row, including cancelled ones) proceeds: attendees are created and a calendar update is attempted on a dead event, and since cancelled/rejected bookings carry null startTime/endTime — exactly what the ternaries at lines 128-129 guard for — the emitted event.ics has empty/invalid DTSTART-DTEND and the emails describe a meeting with no date.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched only by `id` with no status constraint (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and there is no subsequent `booking.status` check before updating attendees and calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` + `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. On the UI side, the new action is added unconditionally to `actions` in `BookingListItem` (no check for cancelled/rejected), so the mutation can be triggered for any booking row the list renders. The constructed `CalendarEvent` explicitly allows empty `startTime`/`endTime` (`booking.startTime ? ... : ""`), which would produce emails/ICS with missing times if such bookings can have null times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The team-member notification loop added here can never execute: the only call site added in this diff (addGuestsHandler) builds its CalendarEvent without a team property, so calendarEvent.team?.members is always undefined. For team event types, non-organizer team members never receive the guests-added notification this branch exists to send — intended recipients are silently skipped with no log and no error while the handler reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the team-member notification branch depends on `calendarEvent.team?.members` after `formatCalEvent(calEvent)`. The only new call site in this diff (`addGuestsHandler`) constructs `evt: CalendarEvent` without any `team` field (it sets organizer, attendees, etc., but no `team` object/members). From the diff alone, that means the `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }` loop will be skipped, so only the single organizer email (`new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })`) is sent and other team members won't be notified. This is silent because the handler still returns success and email sending errors are swallowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BAD_REQUEST message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' is reused for the all-guests-filtered condition, where the emails are actually unique and valid — they were merely already attending or blacklisted. A user who submits an already-invited guest is told their email must be unique and valid, misdirecting them to retype a valid address instead of revealing the guest is already on the booking; after the unguarded calendar-failure path it also misreports an already-persisted add as an input-format error, sending debugging in the wrong direction.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and any in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If *all* submitted emails are filtered out, it throws `new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That error key implies invalid/duplicate formatting, but this branch is also reached when the inputs are valid emails that are simply already attending or blacklisted, so the user-facing message is misleading and incorrect for those cases.
